The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.643 of 2004 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Mavelikkara is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 22.01.2004.

According to the petitioner, on 22.01.2004 at about 05.00 p.m., while he was riding pillion on a motorcycle, a mini lorry bearing Registration No.KL-07-G-3468 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit on the motorcycle.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.6,54,000/- limited to Rs.6,50,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A21.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,67,195/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.
8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

Sreekumaran Potti vs K.Mohanan*(Deleted) on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195011640/
2
9. Heard Sri.R.Padmakumar, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.P.K.Manoj Kumar, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point:
In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
As per the claim petition, the petitioner claimed that the monthly income is Rs.14,000/-, but the Tribunal has fixed his notional income at Rs.6,000/-.

In the proof affidavit, he claimed that he was getting Rs.7,000/- from his job as poojari and he is getting another Rs.6,000/- from his MACA NO. 313 OF 2016 2025:KER:32573 job as faculty in a computer centre.
However, it is to be noted that in the memorandum of appeal, the income claimed by him is only Rs.7,000/-.

Since the petitioner himself was examined as PW1 and he adduced evidence to prove that from his job as poojari, he used to get a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month, I am inclined to fix his notional income at Rs.7,000/-.

11. In the accident the petitioner sustained deglowing injury in left knee, fracture on left candyle,
90% all wound deglaring injury to knee, lateral patelion relinium injured, extensive skin loss of left knee, X-ray shows fracture left knee lateral tpi condyle, lacerated wound anterior aspect 6x4 cm.
12.
As per Exhibit A20 disability certificate the petitioner suffered 12% permanent physical disability.
It was issued by the medical board.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such.
One of the arguments advanced by the learned counsel is regarding the functional disability of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to the learned counsel, the petitioner is a poojari by profession and because of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not continue his job as poojari after the accident.
Therefore, according to the learned counsel, the functional disability of the petitioner is to be taken as 100%.

On the other hand,
the learned standing counsel for the insurer would argue that the functional disability of the petitioner as fixed by the medical board does not require any MACA NO. 313 OF 2016 2025:KER:32573 interference.
13. In order to convince the disability of the petitioner, the learned counsel has produced the petitioner before the Court.
Photograph showing the injuries sustained on his left leg is also produced.
On examination, it appears that even now he finds it difficult to walk freely.
The photograph shows that even now the injuries sustained in the accident on his left knee, was not completely cured.
In Ext.A20 disability certificate, the medical board also noted that he has limitation on flexion and he had difficulty to sit on ground with folded knees and squatting.

Considering the fact that the petitioner is a poojari by profession, his functional disability will be more than what is stated in Ext.A20 and therefore, I am inclined to fix his functional disability at 20%.
14.
On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 25 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.4,23,360/-
Sreekumaran Potti vs K.Mohanan*(Deleted) on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195011640/
3 15.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.18,000/- being the income for 3 months @ Rs.6,000/- and Rs.3,000/- was awarded towards loss of partial earnings.

Considering the nature of the injuries MACA NO. 313 OF 2016 2025:KER:32573 sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 6 months.

Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.42,000/-
(7,000 x 6 months).
Therefore, separate compensation for partial loss of earnings is not required.
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.35,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.5,000/- was awarded, towards 'bystander expenses' Rs.3,000/- was awarded and towards 'extra nourishment' Rs.3,000/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 40 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' , 'bystander expenses' and 'extra nourishment' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.50,000/-, Rs.35,000/-, Rs.6,000/- and Rs.6,000/- respectively.
18.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.6,29,275/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

Medical and miscellaneous 58,715 58,715  expenses
4 Bystander expenses 3,000 6,000  5 Transportation charges and 7,700 7,700  others
6 Extra nourishment 3,000 6,000  8
Pain and sufferings 35,000 50,000 Sreekumaran Potti vs K.Mohanan*(Deleted) on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195011640/
4  9 Loss of amenities 5,000 35,000  10 Compensation for disability 2,33,280 4,23,360  Total 3,67,195 6,29,275  Enhanced to Rs. 2,62,080 20.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.6,29,275/- (Rupees Six Lakh Twenty Nine Thousand Two Hundred and Seventy Five only), less the amount MACA NO. 313 OF 2016 2025:KER:32573 already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 279 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner,
excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
